text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated connection errors from fabric in us-east-1-rack-12. Packet drop spike + node reboots observed. Paging SRE on-call. (rule: infra.net.rdma.loss > 5% for 3m)

maria: seeing large spike in inference 5xxs and a couple of serving pods restarting with CUDA OOM in the last 10m. Notifying CSE for customer impact.

pagerduty: Triggered A1 -> SRE on-call: @cheng.

cheng: acked, joining. Can someone paste the grafana dashboard link?

maria: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panelId=serving_errors&region=us-east-1 — errors up ~12% P50 latency + node restarts on rack-12 hosts.

dustin: grabbing logs from pod serving/model-rt-1. Looks like repeated `cudaMalloc` failures then container restart.

samir: copying log snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T09:04:12Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T09:04:13Z] serving: KV cache miss, attempting remote fetch -> rdma: timeout
[2026-03-15T09:04:13Z] runtime: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at launch
[2026-03-15T09:04:14Z] container: liveness probe failed, killing container
```

alyssa: interesting — pattern: RDMA remote fetch timeout followed immediately by OOM/illegal address. Could be corrupted transfers / retransmit window explosion.

cheng: oncall notes: 1) isolate affected rack 12 from serving cluster 2) throttle KV remote fetch retries to reduce pressure 3) fall back to local model variant if available. I'm handing pager to @dustin.

dustin: taking on-call. I'll coordinate mitigation. First step: cordon rack-12 nodes from k8s serving pool to stop new requests. Running `kubectl label node rack-12-* maintenance=true` and updating router policy to drain live traffic.

infra-ops: FYI we see IB link flapping on switches 12A/12B, firmware reports microburst counters high. Taking a look at switch telemetry.

sre-bot: NOTE: Automated fallback triggered for customer-tier=hosted -> switched to model-variant small-quantized on 3 nodes to reduce memory footprint.

maria: Customer impact: a handful of enterprise customers reported 5xx spikes and some in-flight requests dropped. CS notified customers with temporary mitigation ETA ~30-45m.

dustin: action log: 09:10 cordoned rack-12, 09:12 drained serving pods, 09:14 scaled up local-cpu-variants x6, 09:18 applied KV retry backoff config `RDMA_RETRY_BASE=200ms -> 800ms` in runtime config.

samir: after throttle we still see a subset of pods reporting illegal address errors — possibly inflight retransmits corrupted buffers. I'll add a short restart loop gap to clear stale connections.

alyssa: can we avoid full node reboots? Restarting ib core/drivers might be less disruptive. @infra-ops any objection?

infra-ops: agree, testing a driver reload on a single host first: `modprobe -r mlx5_core && modprobe mlx5_core` — doing on host rack-12-07 now.

maria: monitoring customer-facing metrics. We should prepare a brief for stakeholders: root cause suspected fabric microbursts causing RDMA retransmit storms -> KV fetch retries -> memory pressure -> container OOMs and crashes.

cheng: good summary. Also include mitigations: (a) cordon + drain rack (b) throttle KV retries + increase backoff (c) fallback to local model variant/CPU where appropriate (d) driver reload or switch IB port to spare.

dustin: noticed one node (rack-12-05) still flapping after driver reload. Taking it out of the rotation and marking degraded for hardware investigation. `kubectl annotate node rack-12-05 degraded=yes`

samir: running a health-check script to repro: ```bash
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -sS https://host/serve | jq -r .status || echo "ERR"; sleep 0.2;
done
``` -> intermittent ERRs when cross-node KV fetch invoked. When KV disabled locally, requests succeed.

alyssa: thanks. That aligns with a network-level issue. Can ops escalate to colo for switch replacement if driver reload doesn't stabilize?

infra-ops: standby. If next 20m show continued flaps we'll open a hardware ticket and swap SFPs or move hosts to a healthy top-of-rack.

dustin: live mitigation checklist (in progress):
- [x] cordon/drain rack-12
- [x] throttle RDMA/KV retries
- [x] trigger automated fallback to smaller model variants
- [x] reload IB driver on suspect nodes (partial)
- [ ] move traffic away from rack-12 to spare hosts (manual)
- [ ] hardware swap / colo escalation if flaps continue

maria: CS updated customers with estimated 45m mitigation window, flagged impacted requests for replay where possible.

cheng: can we add a temporary rollout policy to stop cross-node KV fetches globally until infra green? That will increase cost but reduce blast radius. Thoughts?

samir: we can gate cross-node fetches with runtime flag `KV_REMOTE_ENABLED=false` — flipping now in canary.

sre-bot: ACTION: KV_REMOTE_ENABLED=false rolled to 10% canary at 09:28, monitoring.

maria: early telemetry after canary flip: backend 5xxs dropped ~70% for canary traffic, P95 latency increased 8% but stable.

dustin: rolling the flag to 100% now. Expect higher token cost on local CPU variants but better reliability.

infra-ops: after driver reload and port remap on 12A, packetdrop counters decreased on that switch. Switch 12B still showing burst bursts. We're planning to reroute fabric for affected nodes.

cheng: decision: escalate to hardware swap if 12B not stable in 15m. Meanwhile we've mitigated customer impact by fallback and throttles. Preparing incident bridge notes.

maria: drafting post-incident summary and customer timeline. Please add entries to the bridge: root cause hypothesis, sequence, mitigations, next steps, RCA owner.

dustin: I'm the RCA owner. I'll capture detailed logs, packet captures, and timeline. Assigning follow-ups: infra-ops -> hardware validation, runtime -> permanent KV backoff changes, product -> customer communication.

samir: saving packet capture from rack-12-06: `/var/spool/pcaps/rack12-06-20260315.pcap` and uploading to the incident drive.

alyssa: nice work. Post mortem sync tomorrow 10:30 PT. For now keeping the channel open for updates. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-134 created and linked to this thread.

dustin: closing loop for now — traffic shifted off rack-12, KV_REMOTE disabled cluster-wide, IB driver reloads done on majority, hardware ticket prepped. Will reopen if flaps reappear.

maria: thanks team. I'll post the incident summary draft in #postmortems once initial notes land.

(END)
